props.title: Case Closed: The Phantom of Baker Street

sections.content: Case Closed: The Phantom of Baker Street (2002) marks a fascinating intersection of Sherlock Holmes lore and modern technology within the Detective Conan franchise. Like Summer Wars (2009) and Sword Art Online: Ordinal Scale (2017), it explores virtual reality's dangers through a mystery lens. The film cleverly references Arthur Conan Doyle's work while pushing Detective Conan's formula into new territory, trapping Conan and 50 kids in a deadly VR game where failure means real-world consequences.

sections.content: The film's blend of classic detective elements with technological threats echoes other anime mysteries like Perfect Blue (1997) and Paprika (2006), where reality and virtual spaces blur dangerously. The Jack the Ripper storyline within the game world cleverly ties Victorian London to modern Tokyo, much like how Mary and The Witch's Flower (2017) bridges magical and contemporary worlds.

Director Kanetsugu Kodama builds tension by contrasting Conan's usual deductive skills against the unpredictable virtual environment. This approach shares DNA with films like Digimon: Our War Game (1999) and Belle (2021), where young protagonists must solve real-world problems within digital spaces. sections.content: The film's handling of VR technology proved prescient, predating similar themes in works like Ready Player One (2018) and Accel World: Infinite Burst (2016). The way it integrates historical elements into its virtual world creates a unique hybrid of period mystery and sci-fi thriller, similar to how Detective Conan: Zero the Enforcer (2018) blends traditional detective work with modern threats.
